newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks seen up, material to Singapore.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks seen up, material to Singapore.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper stocks will probably rise by at least 3,000 tonnes while some material is reported to be on its way to Singapore, metal traders said on Tuesday.
"It should go up again 3,000 tonnes," the general manager of a European metal trading firm said. "Essentially, it's coming from China."
"Three thousand (tonnes) up is about right," a trader for a Japanese trading company added.
But Vinod Kumar, director of Singapore-based metal firm Donal Mcarthy, predicted that copper stocks may even rise higher.
"Five to six thousand tonnes up is my estimate," he said.
The LME stocks report is due out on Tuesday at 0900 GMT.
Traders said between 4,000 to 5,000 tonnes, most of it from China, may still be on the way to the LME's Singapore warehouse.
"There's still a lot of material to be put on warrant here," Kumar said.

Singapore-based dealers estimate about 20,000 tonnes may remain off warrant. The amount of copper in the LME warehouse was reported at 14,125 tonnes last Friday, 1,625 tonnes up from the previous Tuesday report.
Aluminium stocks are expected to post a small decline in the LME report by about 1,000-2,000 tonnes, dealers said.
Three month copper price was being quoted in Singapore at around US$2,118/23 a tonne at 0745 GMT, down from the late trade in London on Monday of $2,127/30 a tonne.
Aluminium prices were seen hovering at $1,501/06 a tonne at 0745 GMT, also down from the late trade in London yesterday of $1,509 a tonne, traders said.
